summary: Layout of the DjangoLux runtime volume: staged releases and the pointer the supervisor reads at container start.

releases.purpose: One directory per staged release, named for its version; contains the unpacked package.

staging.purpose: Scratch space for a release being assembled before it is moved into releases/.

failed.purpose: Quarantined releases that failed verification or did not come back healthy. Never activated.

state.purpose: Pointer and coordination files shared by DjangoLux and Composer.

active_json.absent_means: The release baked into the project image is in force.
rules: source 'volume' requires path to name an existing directory under releases/
generation is a non-negative integer that increases on every activation
written atomically (temp file in the same directory, then rename)

generation.format: A single non-negative integer followed by a newline.
generation.meaning: Bumped on every activation, including a rollback. The supervisor treats a change as 'the active release moved'.

image-update-request.json.ack.purpose: Terminal token and exit code for the image request.

package-update-request.json.purpose: Intent: apply or roll back an inline DjangoLux release.

package-update-request.json.ack.purpose: Terminal token and exit code for the package request.

deploy-status.json.purpose: Progress and terminal state of the current operation.

mounts.note: Only the executor writes the volume. Application containers mount it read-only and must never create directories.
